chapter: Family and early memories of Jelly
title: No music at home; her grandson the pianist
summary: No piano in grandmother's house; she never learned music, but her grandson plays Erroll Garner and studies piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: of her, too. Did you have a piano in your grandmother's home? No. I wonder. No. Or any other instruments around? No, not that I can remember. Did you ever learn any music? I know you were

interested in music. I did, but I never did learn anything. My grandmother wanted us to be housewives. She taught us how to cook, sew, wash, and take care of babies. She felt like marriage is an institution as well as Annie. Yeah. Well, my grandson plays music now. He's a pianist, and he had—I gave him a piano when he was 12. So he's doing nicely with his music, too. He's 17 now. I'm just hoping that one of them would have something that my brother had, you know what I mean? Some of that challenge. Some of that challenge is right. But I mean, his teacher said he showed such wonderful potentials that really, truly and truly, that she had him the first year playing popular numbers. He plays Eric Garner's Whispering now. Oh, yeah. And—but his new teacher just wants him to play classics only, you know what
I mean? Yes, yes. I studied music. That's all I ever played was classics. Yes. But I got interested in the—
Yes. In the jazz and— And Julie can—she said, just so you know music, you can play any kind once you learn music. Oh, yes. That's right. And he'd be 17 in August, you see, so—
